Irigenin is reported to target 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2B, which in turn is a target of Arecoline. Arecoline, in turn, has a target relationship with Lysosomal phospholipase A2. This indicates a chain of interactions where Irigenin may influence Arecoline's activity, which then affects Lysosomal phospholipase A2. The scores for this pathway are consistent, suggesting a plausible biological link. Additionally, Irigenin is also shown to target another entity, Retinal rod rhodopsin-sensitive cGMP 3',5'-cyclic phosphodiesterase subunit gamma, which is also a target of Arecoline, further supporting the involvement of Arecoline in the pathway. The evidence highlights a possible mechanism by which Irigenin could modulate Lysosomal phospholipase A2, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated. The consistency in scores across the two paths reinforces the likelihood of a functional relationship, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct involvement of Irigenin in this process.
